examples.en: Grandfather heard the joke and laughed heartily.

examples.ko: 아버님은 속이 시원하신 듯이 껄껄 웃으셨어요.
examples.en: Father laughed heartily as if he felt relieved.

examples.ko: 박사님은 제자의 재치 있는 농담에 껄껄 웃으셨어요.
examples.en: The professor roared with laughter at his student's witty joke.

examples.ko: 사장님은 제 실수를 보고도 껄껄 웃고 넘어가셨어요.
examples.en: The boss saw my mistake and just laughed it off.
My uncle always talks with a hearty laugh.

examples.ko: 어르신들이 껄껄 웃으며 옛날이야기를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The elders told us old stories with hearty laughter.

explain: '껄껄 웃다'처럼 쓰고, 어른이 기분 좋게 크게 웃는 호탕한 웃음이 떠오르는 말이에요. 아이들이나 젊은 사람이 높고 경쾌하게 웃을 때는 '깔깔'을 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 할머니가 손주의 이야기를 듣고 껄껄 웃으셨어요.
phrases.en: Grandma listened to her grandchild's story and laughed heartily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이 웃을 때는 '-시-'를 넣어 높여요. 호탕하게 웃는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-시-' when an elder laughs. It describes a hearty laugh.

phrases.en: The boss laughed loudly and offered a handshake.
phrases.nuance_ko: '껄껄'을 세 번 써서 웃음이 계속 이어지는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeating it three times adds the feeling of continued laughter.

phrases.en: The kids are laughing and giggling while watching a cartoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지만 '깔깔'은 아이나 젊은 사람의 높고 경쾌한 웃음이에요. '껄껄'은 낮고 굵은 웃음이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but '깔깔' is a high, bright laugh from kids or young people, while '껄껄' is a deeper, heartier laugh.

explain_en: Used as '껄껄 웃다', it evokes a hearty, good-natured laugh, often of an older person. A high, light laugh of children or young people is usually '깔깔'.

examples.ko: 부모님은 우리를 남부럽지 않게 키워 주셨어요.
examples.en: My parents raised us as well as anyone could.

examples.ko: 남부럽지 않은 직장에 다니는데도 늘 피곤해요.
examples.en: I work at a job anyone would envy, but I'm always tired.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 남부러울 것 없이 행복해요.
examples.en: Right now I'm happy and lack nothing.

examples.ko: 친구들은 제 생활이 남부럽지 않다고 해요.
examples.en: My friends say my life is nothing to envy others for.
Even if my pay is low, I have nothing to envy others for.

examples.ko: 가진 건 없어도 남부럽지 않을 만큼 열심히 살았어요.
examples.en: I had little, but I lived hard enough to be second to no one.

explain: 거의 '남부럽지 않다', '남부러울 것 없다'처럼 부정형으로 써서 '다른 사람에게 뒤지지 않을 만큼 충분하다'는 느낌을 줘요. 누군가를 부러워한다고 말할 때는 '남부럽다' 대신 '부럽다'를 써요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '남부러워요'가 돼요.

phrases.example: 우리 가족은 남부럽지 않게 살고 있어요.
phrases.en: Our family lives comfortably, second to none.
phrases.nuance_ko: '남부럽다'를 가장 자주 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common negative form of 남부럽다.

phrases.en: He grew up wanting for nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부족한 것이 없다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of lacking nothing.

phrases.en: I want to live in a house that's as good as anyone's.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰고 '충분히 좋은'이라는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun, meaning good enough compared with others.

explain_en: It is almost always used in negative forms like '남부럽지 않다' or '남부러울 것 없다', giving the feeling of being as well off as anyone. To say you envy someone, use '부럽다', not '남부럽다'. It is ㅂ-irregular, so it becomes '남부러워요'.

t90.ax: Right now I'm happy and lack nothing.

en: to complain; to grumble; to murmur

examples.en: My friend grumbled to me on the phone for a long time.
It's okay to vent once in a while when things are hard.
My father keeps complaining that his pay is low.

examples.ko: 넋두리할 사람이 없어서 혼자 일기를 써요.
examples.en: I have no one to vent to, so I write in a diary.
Grumbling won't change anything.
Stop grumbling and let's find a way together.

explain: '넋두리를 하다'를 줄여 한 단어로 쓴 말이에요. 불평을 길게 늘어놓는 모습이라 '넋두리하지 말고'처럼 핀잔을 줄 때도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: On hard days, I vent to my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 습관이나 현재 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for habits or the present situation.

phrases.example: 자꾸 넋두리하지 마세요. 같이 방법을 찾아봐요.
phrases.en: Please don't keep complaining. Let's find a way together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불평을 그만하라는 부탁이나 핀잔으로 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a request or rebuke to stop complaining.

phrases.en: Today I want to vent to someone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속상한 마음을 털어놓고 싶다는 바람을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses a wish to pour out upset feelings.

explain_en: It packs '넋두리를 하다' into one verb. Because it pictures long, drawn-out complaining, it often appears in mild scolding like '넋두리하지 말고'.

examples.en: After I took the medicine, the pain eased a little.

examples.ko: 그렇게 화를 내던 아버지도 시간이 지나자 누그러드셨어요.
examples.en: Even my father, who had been so angry, softened as time passed.
Now that it's spring, the cold has eased a lot.
We started talking again in the calmer atmosphere.
When the wind dies down, the boat sets off again.
Your anger will soften as time passes.

explain: '풀리다'와 비슷하지만 화, 추위, 통증, 긴장처럼 세던 것이 약해질 때 써요. 스스로 약해지는 말이라서 누가 일부러 약하게 만들 때는 '누그러뜨리다'를 써요. '들다'가 ㄹ로 끝나서 '누그러드세요'처럼 ㄹ이 빠질 때가 있어요.

phrases.en: With spring, the cold has eased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세던 추위가 스스로 약해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when strong cold weakens on its own.

phrases.en: After I made a joke, the mood softened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딱딱하던 분위기가 부드러워질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a tense mood becomes softer.

phrases.en: Even after taking medicine, the pain doesn't ease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 세던 것이 약해지지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative, it means the strong thing is not weakening.

explain_en: It is close to '풀리다' but fits things that were strong and then weaken, such as anger, cold, pain or tension. It describes something weakening by itself; when someone makes it weaker on purpose, use '누그러뜨리다'. Since '들다' ends in ㄹ, the ㄹ drops before some endings, as in '누그러드세요'.

t90.ax: Your anger will soften as time passes.

en: to be ashamed; to feel shame

examples.en: My skill looks pale in front of my senior.

examples.ko: 그 선수 앞에서는 제 기록이 무색했어요.
examples.en: My record looked pale next to that athlete's.
I ended up crying like a child, as if my age meant nothing.

examples.ko: 화려한 새 건물도 큰 성당 앞에서는 무색해 보여요.
examples.en: Even the fancy new building looks dull next to the big cathedral.
It is so warm today that it hardly feels like winter.

examples.ko: 친구가 쉽게 설명하니 제 말이 무색해졌어요.
examples.en: My friend explained it easily, so my own words felt pointless.

explain: 더 좋은 것 앞에서 내 말이나 실력이 초라해 보일 때 써요. 'A가 무색하다', 'A가 무색할 만큼'처럼 비교 대상 뒤에 붙여요. '창피하다'는 부끄러운 감정이고, '무색하다'는 기대와 안 맞아 겸연쩍은 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 친구의 실력을 보니 제 자랑이 무색해졌어요.
phrases.en: After seeing my friend's skill, my bragging felt hollow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 나은 것을 보고 내 말이 초라해졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when your own words look poor next to something better.

phrases.example: 그 노래는 유명 가수가 무색할 만큼 좋았어요.
phrases.en: The song was so good it made famous singers look dull.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비교 대상이 초라해 보일 정도로 뛰어나다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is so good that the comparison looks poor.
phrases.en_equiv: to the point of putting others to shame

phrases.en: I feel embarrassed because I made a mistake in front of people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무색하다'와 느낌이 가까운 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday word with a feeling close to 무색하다.

explain_en: It is used when your words or skills look poor beside something better. It appears as A가 무색하다 or A가 무색할 만큼. 창피하다 is plain embarrassment, while 무색하다 is the awkward feeling of not living up to the situation.

t90.ax: My skill looks pale in front of my senior.

examples.en: My younger sibling always lights up when getting pocket money.
The team leader was delighted to hear my suggestion.

examples.ko: 그 소식에 모두가 반색하며 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Everyone clapped happily at the news.
Seeing the delighted face, I was happy too.

examples.ko: 너무 반색할 일은 아니니까 차분히 기다려요.
examples.en: It's nothing to get too excited about, so let's wait calmly.

examples.ko: 할머니는 손녀를 보자마자 반색하고 안아 주셨어요.
examples.en: As soon as Grandma saw her granddaughter, she lit up and hugged her.

explain: 반가운 사람을 만나거나 기쁜 말을 들었을 때 기쁨이 바로 드러나는 모습에 써요. '기뻐하다'보다 그 순간의 표정과 반응이 눈에 보이는 느낌이에요. 높일 때는 '반색하셨어요'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 친구는 제 전화를 받고 반색하며 이야기를 시작했어요.
phrases.en: My friend started talking happily after answering my call.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기뻐하면서 다른 행동을 이어서 할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used when someone does another action while showing delight.

phrases.en: Grandfather was delighted when he saw the gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이나 윗사람이 기뻐하는 모습을 높여 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form, used for an elder or superior showing delight.

phrases.en: My little brother was delighted to see the new game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족 사이에서 편하게 말하는 반말 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, informal form used among friends and family.

explain_en: It is used when joy shows right away on meeting a welcome person or hearing good words. Compared with '기뻐하다', you can almost see the expression and reaction at that moment. For honorifics, say '반색하셨어요'.

examples.ko: 이번 시험 문제 예상이 완전히 적중이었어요.
examples.en: My prediction of this exam's questions was a complete hit.

examples.ko: 선생님이 짚어 주신 부분이 적중이라서 점수가 잘 나왔어요.
examples.en: The part the teacher pointed out was spot on, so my score was good.
That fortune-teller is famous for a high hit rate.

examples.ko: 사격 대회에서는 적중 횟수가 가장 많은 선수가 이겨요.
examples.en: In a shooting competition, the athlete with the most hits wins.

examples.ko: 일기 예보의 적중 여부는 내일 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: We'll know tomorrow whether the weather forecast was right.

examples.ko: 그 감독의 작전은 적중 그 자체였어요.
examples.en: That coach's tactic was a perfect hit.

explain: 예상이나 작전이 딱 맞았을 때, 또는 과녁을 맞혔을 때 쓰는 말이에요. 명사로는 '적중률'처럼 합쳐서 쓰는 경우가 많고, 일상에서는 '딱 맞았어요', '들어맞았어요'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: That fortune-teller is famous for a high hit rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상이 맞은 비율을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The rate at which predictions come true.

phrases.en: This match went just as predicted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상이 그대로 맞았다고 짧게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short way to say the prediction came true.

phrases.en: My guess was exactly right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '적중'을 쉽게 바꿔 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual everyday alternative to 'jeokjung'.

explain_en: It is used when a prediction or tactic turns out exactly right, or when a target is hit. As a noun it often forms compounds like '적중률' (hit rate), and in daily talk people also say '딱 맞았어요' or '들어맞았어요'.

t90.ax: That coach's tactic was a perfect hit.

en: to be charmed; to be fascinated; to be enchanted

examples.ko: 광고에 혹해서 필요 없는 걸 샀어요.
examples.en: I was lured by an ad and bought something I didn't need.

examples.ko: 그 말에 혹하지 마세요, 사기일 수 있어요.
examples.en: Don't fall for that, it could be a scam.
Many people were taken in by the sweet words.
I was tempted by the low price and regretted it.
Many people are charmed by his voice.
I'm easily swayed because I'm easily persuaded.

explain: 말이나 사람, 물건에 마음이 끌려 넘어갈 때 써요. 보통 '~에 혹하다' 꼴이고, 좋은 쪽보다 '조심해야 할 유혹'을 말할 때 자주 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '솔깃하다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: I was drawn in by the cheap price and bought it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에 혹하다' 꼴로 끌리게 만든 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '~에 혹하다' to name what pulled you in.

phrases.example: 혹할 만한 제안이라도 한 번 더 생각하세요.
phrases.en: Even if an offer is tempting, think about it once more.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혹할 만한 + 명사'로 마음이 끌릴 만한 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '혹할 만한 + noun' refers to something likely to draw you in.

phrases.en: That sounds tempting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혹하다'보다 가볍게 귀가 기울어지는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It feels lighter than 혹하다, like your ear just perks up.

explain_en: It is used when your heart is drawn to something, such as words, a person or an item, and you give in. It usually appears as '~에 혹하다' and often describes a temptation to be careful about. A similar word is '솔깃하다'.

examples.ko: 칼을 다 갈았으면 숫돌을 물로 깨끗이 씻어 주세요.
examples.en: When you finish sharpening the knife, rinse the whetstone clean with water.
The knife was dull, so I sharpened it on a whetstone.
You have to wet the whetstone before using it.
Grandfather is sharpening a sickle with a whetstone.

examples.ko: 새로 산 숫돌이 아주 잘 갈려요.
examples.en: The whetstone I just bought sharpens very well.
The middle of the whetstone has worn down and become hollow.

explain: 칼이나 낫을 갈 때 쓰는 돌이고 '숫돌에 갈다'처럼 동사 '갈다'와 같이 써요. 요즘은 집에서 칼갈이 도구를 쓰는 경우도 있어요.

phrases.en: Grandfather is sharpening a knife on a whetstone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숫돌에 갈다'를 더 자세히 말한 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fuller form of 숫돌에 갈다.
phrases.en_equiv: to sharpen a knife on a whetstone

phrases.en: I sprinkle water on the whetstone before sharpening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫돌로 칼을 갈 때 먼저 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for what you do first when sharpening with a whetstone.

phrases.en: These days I sharpen knives at home with a knife sharpener.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숫돌'보다 쓰기 쉬운 요즘 도구를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modern tool that is easier to use than a whetstone.

explain_en: It is the stone used to sharpen knives or sickles, and it pairs with the verb '갈다', as in '숫돌에 갈다'. Nowadays some people use a knife sharpener at home instead.

examples.ko: 제 애마는 십 년 된 낡은 소형차예요.
examples.en: My beloved car is an old compact car that is ten years old.
Every weekend I take my trusty car to the sea.

examples.ko: 아버지는 애마를 닦는 데 한 시간이나 써요.
examples.en: My father spends a whole hour washing his prized car.
The knight rode through the forest with his beloved horse.

examples.ko: 애마가 갑자기 시동이 안 걸려서 지각했어요.
examples.en: My trusty car suddenly wouldn't start, so I was late.

examples.ko: 친구가 애마를 빌려줘서 이사를 쉽게 했어요.
examples.en: My friend lent me his beloved car, so the move was easy.

explain: 원래는 아끼는 말(馬)이라는 뜻인데, 요즘 일상 대화에서는 자기가 아끼는 자동차를 장난스럽게 '내 애마'라고 부르는 경우가 더 많아요. 자동차 광고나 기사에서도 자주 보여요. 말을 가리킬 때는 옛날이야기나 역사 이야기에서 주로 나와요.

phrases.en: My trusty car is acting up today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 차를 장난스럽게 부르는 입말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A playful spoken way to refer to one's own car.

phrases.en: I took my trusty car for a drive after a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타다'보다 직접 운전한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More directly suggests driving than 'to ride'.

phrases.en: I traveled around the whole country with my trusty car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 같이한 차에 정을 담아 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses affection for a car you've had for a long time.

explain_en: Originally it meant a horse one treasures, but in everyday talk people more often playfully call their beloved car '내 애마'. You will also see it in car ads and news articles. When it means a real horse, it mostly appears in old tales and historical stories.

examples.en: I dyed a handkerchief with natural dye.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 염료가 빠져서 다른 옷에 물이 들었어요.
examples.en: The dye came out of this garment and stained my other clothes.
Dyes are sometimes obtained from plants or insects.
I bought blue powder at a dye shop.

examples.ko: 염료에 천을 담가 두면 색이 깊게 배요.
examples.en: If you soak the fabric in dye, the color sets deeply.

examples.ko: 공장에서 염료를 함부로 버리면 강이 오염돼요.
examples.en: If a factory dumps dye carelessly, rivers get polluted.

explain: 옷감이나 종이에 색이 스며들게 하는 물질이에요. 그림 그릴 때 쓰는 '물감'은 표면에 칠하고, 염료는 천 속에 배어들어 물들이는 쪽이에요. 발음은 [염뇨]로 'ㄹ'이 'ㄴ'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: Synthetic dyes have vivid colors.
phrases.nuance_ko: '천연 염료'와 반대로 사람이 만든 염료를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Opposite of 'natural dye'; a dye made artificially.

phrases.en: I dissolved the dye in water and soaked the cloth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 염색을 시작할 때 물에 섞는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes mixing the dye into water when starting to dye.

phrases.example: 양파 껍질을 염료로 써서 실을 물들였어요.
phrases.en: I used onion skins as dye to color the thread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 재료를 물들이는 데 사용할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a material is used for dyeing.

explain_en: It is a substance that soaks color into fabric or paper. '물감' used for painting is applied on the surface, while dye soaks into the cloth and colors it. It is pronounced [염뇨], with 'ㄹ' turning into 'ㄴ'.

t90.ax: I bought blue powder at a dye shop.

en: colder part of an ondol room, away from the heat source

examples.en: The warm end of the floor is cozy, but the far end is a bit cold.
The water I left at the cold end of the room froze solid.
I moved my seat to the cold end of the room.

examples.ko: 윗목에서 자면 밤에 추울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you sleep at the cold end, you may feel cold at night.
The blanket at the cold end of the room was chilly.

examples.ko: 방이 넓어서 윗목까지 온기가 잘 안 와요.
examples.en: The room is big, so the warmth doesn't reach the far end well.

explain: 온돌방에서 불을 때는 쪽에서 먼, 상대적으로 차가운 쪽을 말해요. 반대말은 '아랫목'이고, 옛날 집이나 한옥 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: It's cold, so please sit in the warm spot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말이고, 불을 때는 쪽의 따뜻한 자리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite word, meaning the warm spot nearer the heat source.
phrases.en_equiv: the warm part of an ondol room

phrases.en: The room is old, so the far end is cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방 안에서 온도가 낮은 자리를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain which spot in a room is cooler.
phrases.en_equiv: the far end of the room is cold

phrases.en: I pushed the blanket over to the cold end of the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 따뜻한 자리에서 먼 쪽에 둔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means placing something at the side away from the warm spot.
phrases.en_equiv: to push to the cold end

explain_en: In a Korean heated-floor room, it is the side far from the heat source, which stays relatively cold. The opposite is '아랫목', and it often comes up when talking about old houses and hanok.

en: to be dampish; to be damp

examples.en: The basement is damp, so mold has formed.

examples.ko: 그 방은 햇빛이 안 들어서 음습해요.
examples.en: That room gets no sunlight, so it's dank.
Walking through the damp, dark alley was a little scary.
During the rainy season the inside of the house feels clammy.
I open the windows often so it doesn't get damp.
This house is old, so it was always damp.

explain: '축축하다'는 단순히 젖어 있는 느낌이지만, '음습하다'는 어둡고 눅눅해서 기분이 개운하지 않은 느낌까지 담겨 있어요. 지하실이나 골목, 오래된 방처럼 장소에 주로 써요.

phrases.example: 햇빛이 없는 음습한 방에서는 오래 살기 어려워요.
phrases.en: It's hard to live for long in a damp room with no sunlight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어둡고 눅눅한 장소를 꾸밀 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic modifier form for a dark, clammy place.

phrases.example: 비가 온 뒤라 음습한 골목이 더 어두워 보여요.
phrases.en: After the rain, the damp alley looks even darker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 골목이나 지하처럼 햇빛이 안 드는 곳에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits places without sunlight, like alleys or basements.

phrases.example: 이 집은 햇빛이 잘 들어서 음습하지 않아요.
phrases.en: This house gets plenty of sun, so it isn't damp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 어둡고 눅눅하지 않아서 좋다는 뜻을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says a place is pleasantly free of darkness and dampness.

explain_en: '축축하다' just means wet or moist, while '음습하다' also carries a dark, clammy and slightly unpleasant feeling. It is mostly used for places such as basements, alleys and old rooms.
